extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications licensees, small businesses, auction participants, and stakeholders/respondents to FCC rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Defines the SBA and FCC criteria used to classify small entities across many telecommunications services (employee-count and revenue-based thresholds, subscriber-based cable thresholds), auction-eligibility categories (small/very small/entrepreneur), permissible operations for some services, and notes data limitations in estimating small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA small business size standard for Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard for the industry class 'Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)' (NAICS 517312) classifies a business as small if it has 1,500 or fewer employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This SBA employment-based standard is used as the 'closest industry' benchmark for many services (e.g., SMR, Lower/Upper 700 MHz, 3650–3700 MHz, fixed microwave, BRS/EBS). The analysis cites U.S. Census Bureau 2017 firm counts (e.g., 2,893 firms, 2,837 with fewer than 250 employees) and notes the Commission does not collect employee counts for many licensees, limiting precise estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower 700 MHz auction small/very small/entrepreneur revenue thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: For auctions of Lower 700 MHz Band licenses the Commission adopted three small-business groups defined by average annual gross revenues for the preceding three years: 'entrepreneur' = average gross revenues not exceeding $3 million; 'very small business' = average annual gross revenues not exceeding $15 million; 'small business' = average gross revenues not exceeding $40 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These revenue-based categories determine eligibility for bidding credits and installment payments in Lower 700 MHz auctions. The document cites 47 CFR § 27.702(a)(1)-(3) and provides auction results (e.g., counts of winning bidders claiming small business classifications in Auctions 44, 49, 60).

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper 700 MHz auction small/very small revenue thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: For Upper 700 MHz Band auctions the Commission defined a 'small business' as an entity with average gross revenues not exceeding $40 million for the preceding three years, and a 'very small business' as one with average gross revenues not more than $15 million for the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions affect bidding credit/instalment eligibility in Upper 700 MHz auctions (see 47 CFR § 27.502(a)). The analysis references auction outcomes (e.g., winning bidders claiming very small business status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Air-Ground Radiotelephone Service permissible operations requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee may provide any type of air-ground service (voice, broadband Internet, data, etc.) to aircraft of any type and serve commercial, government, and general aviation markets; a licensee must provide service to aircraft and may not provide ancillary land mobile or fixed services in the 800 MHz air-ground spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a regulatory limitation on permissible operations in the Air-Ground Radiotelephone Service (see 47 CFR § 22.99 and Auction 65 fact sheet). Separately, auction small-business definitions for this service used revenue thresholds (small ≤ $40M; very small ≤ $15M, preceding three years).

rubrics_metrics.name: BRS (Broadband Radio Service) auction small/very small/entrepreneur revenue thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: For BRS auctions the Commission adopted three categories based on average annual gross revenues for the preceding three years: 'entrepreneur' = average gross revenues not exceeding $3 million; 'very small business' = average annual gross revenues exceeding $3 million and not exceeding $15 million; 'small business' = average gross revenues exceeding $15 million and not exceeding $40 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These revenue bands determine eligibility for bidding credits/installment payments in BRS auctions. The document reports auction outcomes (e.g., numbers of winning bidders claiming each category) and cites Auction 86 bidder summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: EBS (Educational Broadband Service) small business size standards
rubrics_metrics.description: EBS small business definitions (for the Commission's purposes) are revenue-based over five years: a 'small business' is an entity that, together with affiliates and controlling interests, has average gross revenues not more than $55 million for the preceding five years; a 'very small business' has average gross revenues not more than $20 million for the preceding five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These EBS thresholds include affiliates, controlling interests, and affiliates of controlling interests in the revenue aggregation. The Commission notes auction-related caveats about winning bidders vs. current-in-service small businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satellite Telecommunications SBA small business size standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard for 'Satellite Telecommunications' (NAICS 517410) classifies a business with $35 million or less in annual receipts as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This receipts-based standard is used to estimate the number of small satellite telecommunications providers; U.S. Census 2017 data show firm revenue distributions (e.g., 242 of 275 firms had revenue < $25 million). Commission Universal Service Monitoring Report data used to estimate provider counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Other Telecommunications SBA small business size standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard for 'All Other Telecommunications' (NAICS 517919) classifies firms with annual receipts of $35 million or less as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. Census 2017 revenue data (e.g., 1,039 of 1,079 firms had revenue < $25 million) support the Commission's estimate that the majority of firms in this category are small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cable and Other Subscription Programming SBA small business size standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For 'Cable and Other Subscription Programming' (NAICS 515210) the SBA small business size standard classifies firms with annual receipts less than $41.5 million as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. Census 2017 data (e.g., 378 firms in 2017; 149 with revenue < $25 million) are cited to estimate the proportion of small firms in the industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission cable rate-regulation small cable company and small system thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Commission's own rules for cable rate regulation: a 'small cable company' is one serving 400,000 or fewer subscribers nationwide; a 'small system' is a cable system serving 15,000 or fewer subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission estimates (based on industry data) of the numbers of companies/systems meeting these thresholds are provided (e.g., about 420 cable companies nationally, ~4,139 cable systems). These thresholds are used specifically for cable rate-regulation analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecom Act 'small cable operator' definition and Commission numeric determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Communications Act defines a 'small cable operator' as one that serves in the aggregate fewer than one percent of all subscribers in the United States and is not affiliated with entities whose gross annual revenues in the aggregate exceed $250,000,000. The Commission operationalized this (for the Telecom Act standard) as serving fewer than 498,000 subscribers (aggregate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the percentage-based statutory definition and the Commission's numeric determination are applied when assessing whether a cable operator meets the Telecom Act small-operator standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed microwave services auction small-business eligibility (average gross revenues categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: When bidding credits are adopted for auctions of fixed microwave service frequency bands, such credits may be available to several types of small businesses (small, very small, entrepreneur) based on average gross revenues pursuant to competitive bidding rules and/or Part 101 of the Commission's rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The availability and precise revenue thresholds depend on the specific auction and rule provisions (see 47 CFR §§ 101.538(a)(1)-(3), 101.1112(b)-(d), 101.1319(a)(1)-(2), and 101.1429(a)(1)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No Commission small-business size standard developed for 3650–3700 MHz (3650–3700 MHz statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has not developed a specific small business size standard applicable to 3650–3700 MHz band licensees; based on granted licenses, the Commission estimates that the majority of licensees in this service are small Internet Access Service Providers (ISPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document reports there were 902 active licenses as of November 2021 but notes the Commission does not collect employee counts for these licensees, preventing precise SBA-size qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction-winning bidder small-business status caveat and Commission tracking limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: In frequency bands where licenses were subject to auction, the number of winning bidders that qualify as small businesses at the close of an auction does not necessarily represent the number of small businesses currently in service; the Commission does not generally track subsequent business size unless, in the context of assignments or transfers, unjust enrichment issues are implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an analytic caveat repeatedly applied across services: auction-time small-business claims are not equivalent to current-in-service small-entity counts; the Commission's estimates therefore rely on a combination of SBA standards, Census data, auction records, and limited Commission datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission data limitation: lack of employee-count collection for many licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission does not collect data on the number of employees for licensees providing many of these services; therefore, at this time the Commission is not able to estimate the number of licensees with active licenses that would qualify as small under the SBA's small business size standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodological limitation is cited across numerous service-specific analyses (e.g., SMR, Lower/Upper 700, Air-Ground, 3650–3700 MHz, fixed microwave, BRS/EBS) and informs the Commission's conservative estimation approach (e.g., 'estimates that a majority of licensees can be considered small').
